transcript.content:
Mapped offences: ['Penal Code (Ordinance No. 2 of 1883) s.324 - Voluntarily causing grievous hurt']
Notes: Single charge under s.324 of the Penal Code (Ordinance No. 2 of 1883) for voluntarily causing grievous hurt, arising from an alleged striking of the victim with a wooden crate during a market-day stall dispute, resulting in a fractured arm and ten days of hospitalization. The accused's claim of sudden quarrel without preplanning may engage the Exception to s.300 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) framework or argue for a lesser classification under s.326 read with the Exception, but the present charge is confined to s.324. Supporting evidence is identified: two eyewitness bystanders, hospital admission records, and the recovered wooden crate; chain-of-custody and forensic linkage of the crate to the injury should be confirmed at the next stage, and the exact nature of the fracture (compound/simple, permanent/temporary disfigurement or disability) should be clarified to determine whether an enhanced charge under s.317 or s.320 (grievous hurt defined categories) is more apt. No additional offences are pleaded; elements of intent (voluntariness) and the grievous nature of the hurt are partially evidenced but should be substantiated through medical testimony and witness statements before filing.

case.title: The Market Altercation (Hypothetical)

charges.max_penalty: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine

case.facts: On a market day, a dispute arose between two vendors over a stall boundary. The argument escalated and the accused struck the victim with a wooden crate, fracturing the victim's arm. The accused claims the blow was struck in the heat of a sudden quarrel and without prior planning. The victim was treated at a hospital and discharged after ten days.

evidence.description: Two bystanders who saw the altercation begin and escalate.
Hospital admission record documenting the arm fracture.
The wooden crate recovered at the scene.
